    Subway or taxi?

    Each picked event shows how to get there from the stop before it. Here's the general rule of thumb.

    Subway

    • Most trips longer than a 15-minute walk, especially when there's a direct line.
    • Rush hours (7–10 AM and 4:30–7 PM), and anywhere in Midtown in December. Holiday traffic around Rockefeller Center and Fifth Ave barely moves.
    • Daytime trips to Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

    Taxi or Uber

    • Late at night, roughly after 10 PM, especially from Dyker Heights, the Bronx Zoo or the dinner cruise.
    • When the subway trip needs two or more transfers.
    • When you're dressed up, carrying shopping bags, or it's freezing out.
    • Expect about $15–30 within Manhattan and $40–70 from Brooklyn or the Bronx, more with surge pricing. Trips below 60th St include a small congestion charge.

    Walk

    • Anything under about 15 minutes.
    • Going north or south, 20 streets is about a mile. The avenues are farther apart, roughly 3 to 4 streets' worth each.

    Paying & planning

    • Tap a contactless card or your phone at the turnstile. It's about $3 a ride, and each of you needs your own card or phone.
    • After 12 paid rides in 7 days on the same card or phone, the rest of that week is free.
    • Dec 20 is a Sunday, so the B train isn't running. Use the D. Weekend service changes are common, so check Google Maps that morning.
    • PATH (to Exchange Place) has its own tap-to-pay turnstiles. Metro-North needs a ticket from the TrainTime app.
